The Ottoman Empire surrendered in World War I by signing the Armistice of Mudros on 30 October 1918 [d2][d4][d6][d8]. The armistice was signed aboard the British battleship HMS Agamemnon, anchored in the port of Mudros on the Aegean island of Lemnos [d2][d4]. This agreement ended Ottoman participation in the First World War and effectively marked the dissolution of the once-mighty empire [d2][d9]. Some sources cite 31 October 1918 as the armistice date [d3][d7], which may reflect when it came into force rather than when it was signed, but the overwhelming consensus places the signing on 30 October 1918 [d2][d4][d6][d8].
